title: Common-stage triangles satisfy TR1--TR4; stage inclusions and transition identifications are exact.
statement: Let $S$ be an exact-stage pair datum [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data] over a nonempty directed preorder $I$, with stage categories $C_i$, pair category $P=S.\mathrm{PairCategory}$, additive inclusions $j_i$, exact transitions $T_{ij}$, and the supplied shift comparisons and shift-compatible identifications $\theta_{ij}$. Suppose every pretriangulated category $C_i$ is triangulated, including TR4 [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Keep fixed the given preadditive structure, zero-object structure and additive integer shifts on $P$, as well as all these comparisons. Then there exists a unique pretriangulated structure $t$ on $P$ for which (i) a triangle $V$ is distinguished exactly when $D_S(V)$, (ii) $P$ with $t$ is triangulated, and (iii) every $j_i$, with its supplied shift comparison, is exact. In particular the given identifications $\theta_{ij}:j_jT_{ij}\cong j_i$ are exact natural isomorphisms: both functors are exact and these identifications commute with the specified shifts.

proof.text: Define the distinguished set to be $D_S$. Its isomorphism closure follows by composing the witness triangle isomorphism. For $X=(i,x)$ use the distinguished identity triangle of $x$ in $C_i$. Its image has zero third object: additivity gives $1_{j_i0}=j_i(1_0)=j_i(0)=0$, so every arrow to or from $j_i0$ is zero and it is isomorphic to the chosen zero of $P$. This gives the identity triangle of $X$. For $f:X\to Y$, apply finite-diagram lifting with no selected rows to get $f_m:X_m\to Y_m$ and vertex isomorphisms $\delta_X,\delta_Y$. Choose a distinguished cone $X_m\xrightarrow{f_m}Y_m\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hX_m[1]$ by stage TR1. Conjugate its image by $\delta_X,\delta_Y$ and the identity of $j_mZ$. Its first map is exactly $f$; its other maps are $j_m(g)\delta_Y$ and $\delta_X[1]^{-1}\beta_{m,1,X_m}j_m(h)$. It satisfies $D_S$ by construction. These verify TR1.

proof.text: For any additive functor $F$ with its given shift comparison $\beta$, the image of the signed rotation of $U$ is isomorphic to the signed rotation of its image: the three components are $1,1,\beta_X$. The last triangle equation is the naturality identity $\beta_Y F(f[1])=(Ff)[1]\beta_X$, with negatives preserved by additivity. Inverse rotation has the analogous isomorphism using $\beta^{-1}$ and the shift unit/counit. Now if $V\cong j_i^\triangle U$ with $U$ distinguished, stage TR2 and this explicit rotation isomorphism show $D_S(V^{\mathrm{rot}})$. Conversely apply stage inverse rotation to a witness for $D_S(V^{\mathrm{rot}})$ and cancel rotation with inverse rotation. This proves both directions of TR2 with the prescribed sign.

proof.text: For TR3 give the lifting lemma the two specified distinguished rows $V,V'$, the two specified maps $a:X\to X'$, $b:Y\to Y'$ and the true equation $bf=f'a$. It gives two distinguished rows in one $C_m$ with the shared lifted vertices and the same square equation. Stage TR3 supplies $c_m:Z_m\to Z'_m$ with $c_mg_m=g'_mb_m$ and $a_m[1]h_m=h'_mc_m$. Put $c=\delta_{Z'}^{-1}j_m(c_m)\delta_Z$. Apply $j_m$ to the two stage equations, substitute the recovery formulas and cancel adjacent vertex isomorphisms. For the connecting equation use $d_{X,1}=\beta_{m,1,X_m}^{-1}\delta_X[1]$. The results are $cg=g'b$ and $a[1]h=h'c$. Thus the original maps, rather than replacement maps, complete to a triangle morphism.

source.place: Tag 0145, definition-triangulated-category (TR1--TR4), with Tag 0144, definition-triangle, and Tag 014V, definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories; finite-stage implementation is the docstring of commonStage_verdier_existsUnique in lean/Sheaf/CategoryTheory/StageSystemVerdier.lean lines 36-49.

proof.text: For TR4 start with the three specified distinguished cone triangles of composable $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ and $gf$, sharing the same $X,Y,Z$. Lift all three rows, both maps and the equality defining $gf$ simultaneously. In $C_m$ apply TR4 to these actual three distinguished rows. It gives $a_m:Q_{1,m}\to Q_{2,m}$, $b_m:Q_{2,m}\to Q_{3,m}$, the two required triangle morphisms, and the distinguished row with last arrow $p_{1,m}[1]d_{3,m}$. Define $a,b$ by their $j_m$ images conjugated by the common vertex isomorphisms. Applying $j_m$ to each stage equation and cancelling those isomorphisms gives the required faces with the original maps. Naturality of $\beta$ identifies the last arrow of the new image row with $p_1[1]d_3$: the comparison of the middle shifted object cancels between $p_{1,m}[1]$ and $d_{3,m}$. The remaining row therefore satisfies $D_S$. This is TR4 for the prescribed three cones, without any faithfulness assumption on a transition or inclusion.

proof.text: Steps 1--3 fill the pretriangulated axioms for the fixed zero, addition and shifts; step 4 supplies the octahedral axiom. For every distinguished $U$ in $C_i$, its image satisfies $D_S$ with witness $(i,U)$ and the identity triangle isomorphism. Thus every $j_i$ is exact for its supplied comparison. The transitions were already exact; hence their composites with these inclusions preserve distinguished triangles. The stipulated shift-compatibility equation for $\theta_{ij}$ is unchanged, so these are exact natural isomorphisms. This establishes all existence clauses.

proof.text: If $t'$ also satisfies the displayed criterion, then for every triangle $V$ its membership in the distinguished set for $t'$ is equivalent to $D_S(V)$ and hence to membership for $t$. Extensionality gives equality of these two distinguished sets. For the fixed underlying structures a Pretriangulated record has only this set as data; its other fields are proofs of the axioms, equal by proof irrelevance. Therefore $t'=t$, proving uniqueness.

theorem commonStage_verdier_existsUnique :
    ∃! t : Pretriangulated S.PairCategory,
      (fun [triInst : Pretriangulated S.PairCategory] ↦
        (∀ T : Triangle S.PairCategory,
          T ∈ distTriang S.PairCategory ↔ S.CommonStageDistinguished T) ∧
        IsTriangulated S.PairCategory ∧ ∀ i : I, (S.ι i).IsTriangulated)
        (triInst := t)
